text:
incident-bot: ALERT: 503 surge on /generate for model v3-proto-2026 in prod-us-west-2. Error rate spiked to 18% over 5m. Paging @maya and @jon :rotating_light:

maya: I'm on it. Looking at the dashboard now, I see p50 latency up 2x and queue depth growing on the prototype pool.

jon: Thanks. Customer impact? Any high-value keys getting throttled?

maya: Quick check — about 12 customers with sustained traffic, mostly dev/test but one mid-market account hitting heavy burst tests. No full account outages yet, but errors returned 503/502.

alice: Looping in product for communications. Might need to gate the prototype variant while we stabilize.

maya: Agreed. My hypothesis: new KV cache behavior in the proto variant + recent kernel switch causing memory pressure and evictions. We should stop routing new traffic to it and send traffic to v3-stable-8k.

jon: Options: 1) Steer traffic by config -> route 100% to v3-stable-8k 2) Apply emergency rate limits/quotas on keys hitting proto 3) Disable proto variant at edge. Prefer steering first to avoid churn.

carlos: If we steer, can we do gradual to avoid client errors? Also need to unblock ongoing in-flight requests.

maya: I'll open a mitigation runbook. Taking action now: applying emergency quota on prototype pool and starting a routing divert.

maya: Running: ```redwoodctl route update --from v3-proto-2026 --to v3-stable-8k --percent 100 --env prod-us-west-2```

deploy-bot: deploy job queued. Job id: dj-8841. Applying routing change to load balancers.

jon: While that's rolling, please set a short-term key-level quota for heavy keys to prevent hammering when they switch. Example: limit burst to 10 r/s per key.

maya: Applying emergency quotas: ```redwoodctl quotas set --scope production --variant v3-proto-2026 --rule "burst:10,rate:5/s" --reason "incident 1854009999"```

deploy-bot: quotas applied to pool proto-2026 (scope prod-us-west-2).

maya: Routing change completed. Traffic is now served by v3-stable-8k. Error rate dropped to ~0.8% within 2m. Latency returning to normal.

jon: Good. Can you also shelve the prototype variant so it won't accept traffic even if autoscaling reconnects? Need a safer lock.

maya: Shelving variant now: ```redwoodctl variant shelve v3-proto-2026 --env prod --hold-until 1854017200 --meta "shelved-due-to-memory-evictions"```

deploy-bot: variant v3-proto-2026 flagged as SHELVED. Autoscaler will not attach new instances.

alice: Notifying affected customers now. Crafting short message: "We're routing your traffic to a stable variant after detecting increased errors on a prototype model. No action required; this is to protect your requests." Will send as an in-product banner for any high-traffic keys.

jon: Great. Next: open an incident postmortem ticket and assign to eng-ml and eng-runtime to investigate kernel change and KV caching behavior.

maya: Created ticket INF-2026-411 and assigned to @carlos and @jon. Notes: memory pressure correlates with recent kernel/compilation changes on prototype variants; reproduced locally with long-prefix workloads.

carlos: I'll take the lead on the debug. Can you attach heap dumps and kernel logs?

maya: Uploading artifacts to the incident folder now. Commands I ran, for traceability:
```
# routing revert
redwoodctl route update --from v3-proto-2026 --to v3-stable-8k --percent 100 --env prod-us-west-2
# quotas
redwoodctl quotas set --scope production --variant v3-proto-2026 --rule "burst:10,rate:5/s" --reason "incident 1854009999"
# shelve
redwoodctl variant shelve v3-proto-2026 --env prod --hold-until 1854017200 --meta "shelved-due-to-memory-evictions"
```

jon: Handing off on-call to @alice for the next 30m while I coordinate with runtime team. If anything regresses, page me immediately.

alice: Taking on-call. I'll monitor error rate and customer feedback. If errors spike above 2% or any SLA breaches, I'll escalate.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 1854009999 status: Mitigated -> traffic moved to stable variant; prototype shelved; quotas applied. Response lead: maya. Severity: S2.

alice: Scheduled a canary-only redeploy of the kernel change to staging and a targeted regression test for long-prefix sequences. Will hold any prod rollout until root cause is confirmed.

jon: Thanks all. Action items summarized in the ticket. We should consider an automated safety check to prevent prototype variants from receiving >5% prod traffic without an explicit opt-in.

carlos: +1 on safety gate. I'll propose a control in runtime. For now, I'll dig into the heap dumps and start a bisect on the kernel switch.

alice: I'll keep updates here and in the incident ticket. Closing Slack loop for now — monitoring. :white_check_mark:
